name: Revised tax invoice
definition: A revised tax invoice is issued under rule 53 by a person whose registration took effect before the certificate of registration was issued, covering taxable supplies made in that gap. Rule 53(1) lists the particulars, (a) to (j), and clause (a) requires the words 'Revised Invoice' to be shown prominently.
why_it_exists: Registration can be backdated. Supplies made in the gap were invoiced without a GSTIN. The revised invoice re-documents them, which is why it must point at the original document it revises.
inputs: the date of issuance of the certificate of registration
the original tax invoice or bill of supply being revised
outputs: the set of rule 53(1) particulars found
the set of mandatory particulars absent
preconditions: registration was granted with effect from a date earlier than the date the certificate was issued
exceptions: a consolidated revised tax invoice may be issued for all supplies to one unregistered recipient in the period
for inter-State supplies not exceeding two lakh fifty thousand rupees, a consolidated revised invoice may be issued per State for unregistered recipients
common_mistakes: using a revised tax invoice to correct a price or a tax error — that is a credit or debit note under section 34
issuing one without the words 'Revised Invoice' shown prominently
omitting the serial number and date of the document being revised, which clause (h) requires
legal_references: UNKNOWN — section 31 of the CGST Act, which rule 53 refers to, was not read for this record
gst_references: UNKNOWN — source is the Rules as at 01-01-2022; later amendments not held locally

UNKNOWN — in this compilation the words 'and credit or debit notes referred to in section 34' in rule 53(1), and clauses (c) and (i), are bracketed with footnote markers 118, 119 and 120, each reading 'Omitted vide Notf no. 03/2019-CT dt. 29.01.2019 wef 01.02.2019'. Whether those words therefore stand omitted from rule 53(1) is an interpretation of the compilation's bracket convention and REQUIRES HUMAN ACCOUNTANT before any validation depends on it
evidence_required: the certificate of registration and its effective date
the original invoice or bill of supply
confidence_factors: weak when the original document being revised cannot be located
weak because the amendment status of clauses (c) and (i) is unresolved in this source
validation_checks: clause (h) names the serial number and date of the corresponding tax invoice or bill of supply
the supplies fall between the effective date of registration and the date the certificate was issued
examples: a document headed 'Revised Invoice' naming original invoice 44 dated 2 June, issued after a certificate of registration effective 1 June
counterexamples: a document headed 'Revised Invoice' that names no original document — clause (h) fails
